newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Alusuisse gains ahead of July 4 briefing.
newsitem.headline: Alusuisse gains ahead of July 4 briefing.

text.p: Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG shares bucked the weak trend among Swiss stocks and rose on Monday amid speculation the company could announce it is spinning off a division or unifying its shares at a briefing on July 4, analysts said.
Registered shares were off highs but still up 21 Swiss francs to 1,521 by mid-afternoon, extending a recent rally. Bearer shares were up 21 to 1,500.
Analysts said a spin-off was conceivable but not urgent, noting Alusuisse's three core businesses of aluminium, chemicals and packaging were all performing well.

"Should part of Alusuisse get a public listing, then that would be like Sulzer," said Patrick Hasenboehler at Zuercher Kantonalbank, referring to Sulzer's flotation of a minority stake in its Sulzer Medica unit.
"A flotation like Sulzer's would be possible, but Alusuisse would remain a conglomerate," which investors would not appreciate, added Werner Richli from CS Equity Research.

Another stock watcher at a Swiss bank who asked not to be identified said the current boom on the Swiss bourse argued for a public offer of part of the Alusuisse group, perhaps a minority stake in its Lonza chemicals division.

He was not convinced by comment last week from Andrea De Virgiliis, a member of Lonza's management board, who said Alusuisse did not plan to sell any of its core businesses. "Chemicals are hot at the moment," the analyst said.

He added Lonza was too small to be a major player but too big to be a niche specialist. Selling off a stake could raise money for other purposes, for instance beefing up packaging operations in Asia or expanding the biotechnology business.
This analyst suggested Lonza could merge with Ciba Specialty Chemicals or Ems Chemie at some stage.
Patrick Huber, analyst at Societe Generale Bank & Trust, said a joint venture in the aluminium area would make sense because Alusuisse needed to build critical mass there.
He wondered whether it should limit its role to that of an automotive supplier and give up its own bauxite mining.
Packaging was the least likely area to be shaken up.
"After Alusuisse's acquisition of Lawson Mardon, this segment is just where it should be," Huber said.
Other analysts played down the prospects for spectacular developments and believed the briefing could just go over new chief executive Sergio Marchionne's strategic vision.

"In principle Alusuisse should still consist of three divisions after July 4," said Ivo Hanusch at UBS Global Research. He thought Marchionne could set new targets for cash flow, earnings per share or return on net operating assets.

Lorenz Reinhard at Bank Julius Baer said he expected the company to give more information about long-term prospects for the three sectors. This might be sweetened with news of a unified share category or a reduction in shares' par value.

Should nothing dramatic emerge from the briefing, Alusuisse shares could come under pressure. Since June 17, registered shares have climbed from 1,435 to a high of 1,534. Bearer shares soared to a high of 1,517 from 1,445 on June 16.
